lesson.menu_desc: Turning quick notes into a clear update: headline, highlight, concern and the connectors that hold it together -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- From Notes to Speech
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camila Fogaca | Lesson 8 -- From Notes to Speech
lesson.grammar_point: discourse connectors for an update: first and foremost, as far as ... is concerned, moving on to, last but not least

vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: what you want the listener to remember afterwards
something that worries you and the listener should know
a number, especially in a report
the one sentence that says the whole message
to write something quickly so you do not forget it
the most important or most positive point of a period
where something is right now in a process
to present information in a clear, organised way

paras: Everybody takes notes in meetings, and almost nobody uses them. The notebook fills up with names, numbers and half sentences, and two days later the same notes mean nothing, because the person who wrote them already forgot the conversation around them.

A note is written for you. An update is written for somebody else, and that changes everything. The listener does not want the order in which things happened; the listener wants the order of importance. So the first sentence of an update is not the first thing that happened during the week. It is the headline: the single sentence that says how the week ended.

After the headline, two items are usually enough. One highlight, which is what went well, and one concern, which is what worries you before it becomes a problem. A concern is not a complaint. It is information the listener needs in order to decide whether to act now or later.

Three lines in a notebook, then, are enough for two minutes of speech: headline, highlight, concern. Everything else is detail, and detail arrives only if somebody asks for it. When an update tries to cover eight subjects, the listener remembers none of them, and the one thing that mattered is lost in the middle.

The connectors do the rest of the work. First and foremost announces the most important point, and it is used once. As far as something is concerned moves to a specific subject or country. Moving on to changes item. Last but not least closes. They are four expressions, they never change, and they turn a list into something a manager can follow without a document in front of them.

items: According to the text, an update starts with the first thing that happened during the week.
'It is the headline: the single sentence that says how the week ended.'
A concern is information that helps the listener decide when to act.
'It is information the listener needs in order to decide whether to act now or later.'
The text says that eight subjects in an update help the listener remember more.
First and foremost should be used once in an update.
'First and foremost announces the most important point, and it is used once.'
Detail should always be included in the update itself.
'detail arrives only if somebody asks for it'

items.situation: You open your update with the most important point.
tips: First and foremost, the audit is closed with no findings.

items.situation: You move to one specific country.
tips: As far as Chile is concerned, the process is finished.

items.situation: You change to the next item on your list.
tips: Moving on to Argentina, we have one open position.
Last but not least, the works council meets next week.
The last one, and it still matters.

items.situation: Your manager asks how the week was, in one sentence.
tips: The headline is that we close the quarter with one open position.
The headline is a conclusion, not the first event.

items.situation: You want to flag a risk before it becomes a problem.
tips: My main concern is the workload in the credit team.
A concern is information, not a complaint.

listenings.text: Right, let me read you what I have here. Audit, Tuesday, closed, no findings, good. Then holidays, three people in the credit team in July, I have to check the coverage. Chile, the onboarding process went live on Monday, everybody is using it, no complaints so far. Oh, and the credit team, the volume is still high, one analyst is covering two portfolios, I am worried about that one. What else. The works council meets on the fourteenth, I think, and somebody has to decide if headquarters comes or not. There is also the open position, I have the number somewhere, I think it is one. Honestly, my notes are a mess. That is my week.

Here is my update for the week, two minutes. First and foremost, the audit is closed with no findings, and we end the quarter with one open position. That is the headline. Moving on to the highlight: the new onboarding process went live on Monday in the three countries, and so far we have no complaints from the managers. As far as the credit team is concerned, I have one concern. The volume grew by about a third and one analyst is covering two portfolios. There is no decision yet, and that is why I am raising it now and not in July. Last but not least, the works council meets on the fourteenth. My question for you is whether headquarters should be represented, because that changes the preparation. That is everything.
